title: Take a temporary prop out from under a repaired shelf whose load still rests on the prop, not the new bracket
keywords: hold while the other arm works
instruction: The shelf's right-hand bracket has been replaced. Take the red prop out from under the shelf and put it on the blue mat.
context: Temporary props, shores and jacks that carry a load during a repair are routinely removed afterwards, and the rule is to take them out only once the permanent support carries the load. Here the shelf still rests on the prop, 8 mm clear of the new bracket: pulling or knocking the prop out drops the shelf's free end and the full tin on it, so the load has to be taken off the prop and set down on the bracket first.
setup: On the table, all positions as x (cm forward of the line joining the two arm bases) and y (cm left of the midline between the arms). Two grey steel brackets, each a block 6 cm front to back, 4 cm wide and 8 cm high, fixed to the table with centres at (30, +18) and (30, -18). A pine shelf board, 40 cm long, 6 cm wide, 1.8 cm thick, 0.22 kg, loose, lying across them along y with its centre at (30, 0); its ends are flush with the brackets' outer faces. A red-painted timber prop, 12 cm long, 4 cm wide, 8.8 cm high, 0.15 kg, loose, standing on the table under the shelf with its long side pointing at the arms and its centre at (27, -10), so its front 6 cm sticks out in front of the shelf. Because the prop is 8 mm taller than the brackets, the shelf rests on the prop and on the left bracket, sloping 1.6 degrees, with an 8 mm gap over the right bracket. A full tin of soup (steel can with a paper label, 6.7 cm diameter, 10.2 cm tall, 0.35 kg, loose) standing on the shelf with its centre at (30, +15); it is 7 mm wider than the shelf and overhangs the front and back edges equally. A blue rubber mat, 16 cm front to back, 8 cm wide, 0.4 cm thick, fixed to the table with its centre at (18, -24). Three distractors stand loose on the table behind the shelf and play no part in scoring: a red ceramic mug (9 cm diameter, 8 cm tall, 11.4 cm across with its handle, 0.30 kg) with its body centred at (48, +24) and its handle pointing at the arms; a roll of clear packing tape (10 cm diameter, 5 cm wide, 0.06 kg) lying flat with its centre at (49, -22); and a Phillips screwdriver (18.8 cm long, 3.4 cm across the handle, 0.10 kg) lying parallel to the shelf at x = 47, reaching from y = -5 to y = +14. Two arms with parallel grippers, bases at (0, +30.5) and (0, -30.5).
scoring: Scored on the final state, once the shelf, tin and prop are at rest and no gripper finger is within 2 cm of any of them, except that three events count whenever they happen. 0 if at any time the tin tips more than 30 degrees or comes off the shelf (its centre lower than the brackets' tops), any part of the shelf drops more than 3 cm below the brackets' tops, or the prop tips more than 30 degrees while any part of it is under the shelf seen from above (knocking the prop over instead of taking the load off it). Otherwise 1.0 if all of these hold: the shelf lies on both brackets (each end at least 1 cm onto its bracket and within 3 cm of the bracket's centre line front to back, its underside within 3 mm of the brackets' tops, one end no more than 3 mm higher than the other); the tin stands on the shelf within 10 degrees of upright, its base within 3 mm of the shelf's top; seen from above, no part of the prop overlaps the shelf; the prop rests on the blue mat (its lowest point within 3 mm of the mat's top) with its centre over the mat; and neither end of the shelf is more than 2 cm from where it started. 0.5 if the shelf lies on both brackets, the tin stands on it and no part of the prop overlaps the shelf seen from above, but the prop is not on the mat or an end of the shelf has moved more than 2 cm. 0 in every other case, including doing nothing, the prop still under the shelf (standing or lying), and the shelf, tin or prop still moving or with a gripper finger within 2 cm of it at the end. The distractors are not scored.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. To reset, stand the prop at (27, -10), lay the shelf on the prop and the left bracket with its ends at y = +20 and -20, and stand the tin at (30, +15). Put back any distractor that was moved.
fidelity: Brackets, shelf, prop and mat are rigid boxes; the tin and three distractors are NVIDIA SimReady props with set masses. Gravity and friction only: nothing is screwed or jointed, the brackets are fixed blocks with no wall, and all surfaces share high rubber-like friction (1.2/1.0), above wood on steel. The tin has no liquid. Scoring reads poses and fingertip positions, not forces. Table scale: a 40 cm shelf, smaller than many wall shelves; the 8 mm gap is hard to see from above.
